title: QUICK PRO TR One - Personal review

takeaways.text: Quick Pro offers SRAM Red, Dura-Ace and SRAM Rival builds; his Rival bike with RORE 88 mm front and disc rear wheel cost about ¥35,000 at a Shanghai dealer and weighs a little over 8 kg.
It comes with 28 mm GP5000s, a saddle he finds comfortable, interchangeable extension angles (10°, 20°, 25°) and stack adjustment via four bolts, plus integrated hydration and storage.
More comfortable than his previous-generation Specialized Shiv and fast: he holds about 5 km/h more than on his Tarmac at the same power.
Niggles: the between-the-arms bottle mount points downward with no shims to level it, and no aero grips or blip mounts are supplied.

disclosure: Owner bought from a Quick Pro dealer in Shanghai; his complete bike is the SRAM Rival build with a disc wheel, not the candidate's Dura-Ace Di2 build.
summary: An owner's review of a size-M Quick Pro TR:ONE after about 200 km including a time trial.
